title: The world’s first commercial wet dock, buried under a shopping centre
episode: The Old Dock: Hidden history beneath your feet
spotify: National Museums Liverpool Podcast The Old Dock: Hidden history beneath your feet
apple: National Museums Liverpool Podcast The Old Dock: Hidden history beneath your feet
description: Thomas Steers’s Old Dock opened in 1715 as the world’s first enclosed commercial wet dock, was filled in during the 1820s and rediscovered in 2001 beneath what is now the Liverpool ONE shopping district. National Museums Liverpool tells its story.

title: The port that made Liverpool, and the warehouses built not to burn
spotify: Dan Snow's History Hit Liverpool's Historic Docks
apple: Dan Snow's History Hit Liverpool's Historic Docks
description: Historian Dan Snow on Liverpool’s docks, which made it Britain’s great Atlantic port. Their showpiece is the Royal Albert Dock, Jesse Hartley’s 1846 ring of iron, brick and stone warehouses built so that nothing in them could catch fire.

title: How a city remembers the trade that built its wealth
episode: Remembering the Slave Trade in Liverpool
place: International Slavery Museum, Royal Albert Dock
spotify: Realms of Memory Remembering the Slave Trade in Liverpool
apple: Realms of Memory Remembering the Slave Trade in Liverpool
description: By the late 1700s Liverpool was Britain’s leading slaving port. This episode looks at how the city has come to remember that past, including the International Slavery Museum, opened on the waterfront in 2007 for the bicentenary of abolition.

title: Four Liverpool teenagers and the cellar club where it started
spotify: The Rest is History The Beatles
apple: The Rest is History The Beatles
description: Historians Tom Holland and Dominic Sandbrook on the Beatles, who played the Cavern Club, a cellar club on Mathew Street, close to 300 times in 1961–63. The original cellar was filled in in 1973; today’s club is a rebuilt version a few yards away.

title: Ninety-seven fans, a cover-up and a city’s long fight for the truth
spotify: History Daily The Hillsborough Stadium Disaster
apple: History Daily The Hillsborough Stadium Disaster
description: Lindsay Graham recounts the 1989 FA Cup semi-final crush at Sheffield’s Hillsborough stadium that killed 97 Liverpool fans, and the police smears that followed. Inquests in 2016 found they were unlawfully killed. Their memorial stands at Anfield stadium.
